heroLead: Alpena runs on limestone, the cement plants along the bay have driven the local economy for over a century, but the oil and gas mineral rights under the farm ground around town are a separate, real story worth checking.
intro: Alpena, the county seat, sits on Lake Huron and is best known for the limestone quarrying and cement production that's anchored its economy for generations. Oil and gas leasing and drilling reached the farm and forest sections around Alpena too, tied to Traverse Group and Devonian reef trends running through the Michigan Basin, separate from the county's dominant limestone extraction industry.

sections.heading: Limestone rights and oil and gas rights aren't the same thing
paragraphs: Because quarrying has been such a dominant industry here, some Alpena-area deeds carry layered mineral history, surface rights, limestone or aggregate rights, and oil and gas rights that may have been severed from each other at different points by different owners. If your family's paperwork only mentions one type, it's worth checking whether the others were addressed separately, since they're valued in completely different ways.

sections.heading: What an Alpena-area oil and gas interest is worth
paragraphs: Alpena sits outside the Antrim Shale core, so any oil and gas production tied to your interest more likely connects to Traverse Group or Devonian reef formations, with activity that varies a lot by specific section rather than following a uniform county pattern. We check your actual statements and current production before quoting anything, and we're upfront if your interest was only ever leased rather than actually drilled.

sections.heading: What we need to evaluate an Alpena interest
paragraphs: Send us your deed or probate document, any royalty statements or division orders you've received, and note whether your paperwork references limestone, aggregate, or oil and gas specifically. That distinction changes how the interest gets valued from the start.

Given how much of Alpena's mineral history runs through farm and homestead land passed down over generations, it's common for an owner to come to us without the full picture. We can help trace what's recorded before you decide anything.

faqs.question: My deed mentions limestone rights. Do I also own oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Some Alpena County deeds separate limestone or aggregate rights from oil and gas rights, severed at different times by different owners. Pulling the full recorded chain at the county register of deeds will clarify it.

faqs.question: Is Alpena part of the Antrim Shale trend?
faqs.answer: No, Alpena County sits outside the Antrim core. Oil and gas history here ties more to Traverse Group and Devonian reef trends in the Michigan Basin.

faqs.question: How do I check whether my Alpena-area mineral interest has ever produced?
faqs.answer: Contact any operator listed on past correspondence for a division order, or check the Alpena County register of deeds for recorded leases tied to your parcel.

faqs.question: Is a mineral interest near Alpena worth anything if there's no active well?
faqs.answer: It can carry some value tied to future leasing potential, but that's a more speculative situation than an interest with an active production history. We'll tell you plainly which category your interest falls into.
